title: Raw HTML and html_safe Misuse
platform_conditions: Ruby 3.x; MRI — the html_safe flag is a plain String property; escaping layers honor it wherever the string is rendered
security_mechanism: String#html_safe flips a trust flag on the String so the rendering layer skips HTML escaping for it; calling it on anything derived from input (or passing input through raw()) hands attacker bytes to the response as markup. The flag is not contextual: a string marked safe is emitted unescaped in body, attribute and script contexts alike, so single-quote or attribute-boundary payloads survive. A separate attribute-context hazard survives even correct HTML escaping: a javascript: URL placed into an href/src attribute executes on click because the text itself needed scheme validation, not escaping.

source_sink_clues.source: User-supplied text fields, bios, comments and URLs rendered into HTML responses.
source_sink_clues.sink: html_safe / raw() applied to input-derived strings; unescaped interpolation into attribute contexts; javascript:-scheme URLs placed into href/src attributes

tracking_guards: Require that html_safe/raw is never called on input-derived strings — only on server-generated constant HTML; require allowlist-based sanitization (tag/attribute whitelists) before any HTML must be allowed; require URL scheme validation (http/https/relative only) before placing values into href/src.
not_candidate_when: The marked string is a server-side constant template fragment, input passed through a real allowlist sanitizer before being marked safe, or URL attributes are scheme-validated before rendering.
public_references: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html
OWASP Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
